question: Can a large crowdsourced dataset of student-teacher information-seeking dialogs over hidden Wikipedia text expose challenges in contextual, open-ended, unanswerable question answering that existing reading comprehension data miss?
hypothesis: Models built for this data must incorporate dialog context to perform well; strong SQuAD-style models without context will fall well short of humans.
contributions: QuAC: 14K information-seeking QA dialogs (100K questions) with information asymmetry between student and teacher
Dialog acts (continuation, affirmation, answerability) as part of the answer
Baselines including context-aware BiDAF++ with a 20 F1 gap to humans

method.summary: Two Mechanical Turk workers play student (sees only section title and first paragraph of the article) and teacher (sees full section, answers with a span up to 30 tokens plus dialog acts). Baselines (sanity checks, text-matching, logistic regression, BiDAF++ with and without k previous QA pairs) are evaluated with word-level F1 and HEQ.
method.task: information-seeking conversational extractive QA with dialog acts

datasets.name: QuAC
datasets.split: train/dev/test 83,568/7,354/7,353 questions; 11,567/1,000/1,002 dialogs; no sections shared across folds; train has 1 reference, dev/test 5 references; questions with human F1 < 40 excluded from evaluation (~10%)
datasets.source: Wikipedia sections about people (>=100 incoming links, non-person entities removed with YAGO), collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk; http://quac.ai
datasets.preprocessing: Sections filtered by number of paragraphs, tokens, average words per sentence; max answer length 30 tokens; dialogs with <3 QA pairs discarded; dialog ends at 12 questions, partner quit, or >2 unanswerable questions; no-answer kept only if majority of references mark it

models.name: BiDAF++ (no ctx)
models.architecture: BiDAF + self-attention (Clark and Gardner 2018) + contextualized embeddings (ELMo); no-answer token appended to section; dialog-act classifier over the span-end representation

other.note: AllenNLP re-implementation, 82.7 on SQuAD dev vs 85.8 reported

models.name: BiDAF++ w/ k-ctx
models.architecture: BiDAF++ with marker embeddings on previous k answers in the passage and turn number encoded in question embedding
models.context: previous k QA pairs, k in 1,2,3

models.name: Feature-rich logistic regression
models.architecture: Vowpal Wabbit; n-gram overlap, position/length bias, contextual features

models.name: Pretrained InferSent
models.architecture: sentence with highest cosine similarity to question

other.note: No training hyperparameters stated for any baseline; implementation in AllenNLP

inference.samples: inferred: single run per system; no seeds or variance reported

other.input: first k gold questions and answers, entity, topic, background paragraph, section text, question k+1; predict span indices and dialog acts

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: word-level F1 as in SQuAD after removing stopwords; no-answer scored 1/0; max over references; human computed as average of max F1 over each n-1 subset against heldout reference

metrics.name: HEQ-Q
metrics.definition: % of questions where system F1 >= human F1

metrics.name: HEQ-D
metrics.definition: % of dialogs where system F1 >= human F1 on every question

metrics.name: Dialog act accuracy
metrics.definition: accuracy vs majority annotation, ties random (yes/no affirmation and follow-up continuation)

eval.protocol: dev/test cells reported; exact match not used because span boundaries are vague

limits: Article selection biases data toward entertainers (footnote 6, datasheet)
Answers restricted to spans of at most 30 tokens, limiting expressivity
Training sections are shorter and have one reference; dev/test have five
Evaluation excludes questions with human F1 < 40 (~10% noisiest); unthresholded F1 given in last column
Continuation act has no multiple annotations so no human agreement
No training hyperparameters, seeds or variance reported for baselines
Dated: baselines are 2018 BiDAF++ models; LLM-era models not evaluated

terms.definition: human equivalence score: percentage of examples for which system F1 exceeds or matches human F1 (HEQ-Q per question, HEQ-D per dialog)
